questions.title: Visual protest material as empirical data
questions.question: Which analysis method is applied to the visual protest material?
questions.answer: The analysis method applied to the visual protest material includes first impression analysis, which categorizes the material based on its primary messages, represented objects and individuals, style elements, and type of production [3]. This approach helps identify differences concerning orientation and disposition among protesters by examining these visual characteristics [2].

questions.title: Visual protest material as empirical data
questions.question: Why is triangulation of methods mentioned?
questions.answer: Triangulation of methods is mentioned to enhance the reliability and depth of research findings by incorporating multiple data sources. The paper suggests that visual studies can complement other methods such as interviews and statistical outcomes, providing additional insights [1]. It also emphasizes that visual analysis can support or reject interpretations, making it a valuable tool in the triangulation process [2].

questions.title: Networks of Conflict and Cooperation
questions.question: What role do civilian networks play in conflict?
questions.answer: Civilian networks play a significant role in conflict by influencing both the likelihood and duration of intrastate conflicts [3]. They are crucial in recruitment into armed groups, as social ties to insurgents can increase an individual's likelihood of joining [4]. Additionally, civilian networks affect whether rebels attempt to control territory, depending on their ability to collectively act [1].

questions.title: Transition Design: A Proposal for a New Area of Design Practice, Study
questions.question: What is cosmopolitan localism?
questions.answer: Cosmopolitan localism is a lifestyle-based vision described as small, diverse, local, and place-based communities that are global in their awareness and exchange of information and technology [1]. It emphasizes a balance between being rooted in local contexts while maintaining a global perspective and engagement [2].

questions.title: Breaking the bubble: A case study on the echo chamber effect in Instag
questions.question: Which Instagram features does the study examine?
questions.answer: The study examines several Instagram features including personalised feeds, the Explore page, and targeted content [1]. These mechanisms are analysed to understand how they contribute to the echo chamber effect by amplifying selective exposure and confirmation bias.

questions.title: QUANTIFICATION OF ECHO CHAMBERS: A METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK CONSIDERIN
questions.question: What does the framework extend to?
questions.answer: The framework extends well-established homophily measures to accommodate similarities based on cosine distance for quantifying political ideology in multi-party systems [2]. It also applies this framework to a dataset from the German Federal Election of 2017 to evaluate the approach and demonstrate its outcomes [1].

questions.title: Unveiling Community Dynamics on Instagram Political Network
questions.question: How does the paper model the Instagram commenter interactions?
questions.answer: The paper models Instagram commenter interactions through a probabilistic model designed to extract the backbone of the interaction network [2]. This approach allows for identifying salient interactions based on a null model that captures unexpected interactions among commenters [1]. The methodology focuses on uncovering communities within these interactions, highlighting patterns of coordination and engagement [1].

questions.title: Unveiling Community Dynamics on Instagram Political Network
questions.question: Which community detection method is used?
questions.answer: The Louvain algorithm is used for community detection. This method maximizes modularity to identify non-overlapping sets of nodes representing communities within the backbone network [2].

questions.title: Measuring Networks in the Field
questions.question: Why do small samples cause problems when measuring networks?
questions.answer: Small samples cause problems when measuring networks because as network features become more intricate and depend on how others relate to more people, samples perform worse [1]. This is due to the interconnected nature of observations in a network, which means that well-established practices from non-network survey settings can lead researchers astray [4].

questions.title: Simple changes to content curation algorithms affect the beliefs peopl
questions.question: How was the content inventory created?
questions.answer: The content inventory was created by having participants engage with different argumentative posts pertaining to a range of topics in Study 1 [1]. This process involved sampling and ranking posts for use in subsequent studies, specifically Study 2, where these posts were used in belief updating tasks.
